sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation on account of death of Thulasi Kumar, in a road accident.
2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, are as follows:

On 9.2.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., the deceased Thulasi Kumar was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing No. KA-08-X-8489 as a pillion rider and when he was going near Karahalli, on Karahalli- Thammenahalli road, Bangarpet Taluk, Kolar District, the rider of the said vehicle has ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and fell down.
Due to the impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, but in spite of best treatment the deceased succumbed to the said injuries on 11.2.2022.
The petitioners have spent Rs.5,00,000/-towards medical expenses, transportation of dead body and other incidental expenses.
At the time of accident, the deceased was working as team leader and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically, they have lost their bread earner.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 & 3 are the parents of the deceased, have lost their beloved care taker.

The respondent No.1 is the owner,
respondent No.2 is the insurance policy holder and respondent No.3 is insurer of said vehicle
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 & 2 remained absent hence, they were placed exparte.

sentences.text: Respondent No.3- insurance company appeared through their counsel and filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-08-X-8469 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that at the time of accident the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation as claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence the respondent No.3 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Thulasikumar died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 9.2.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. on Karanahalli- Thammenahalli road, near Karahalli village, Bangarpet Taluk, Kolar District due to the rash and negligence riding of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-08-X-8489 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the first petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
Also examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P14 & 15.

Respondent examined two witnesses as RW.1 & 2, through them got marked Ex.R1 to 4.
6.
Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the material evidence that is available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

sentences.text: The petitioners to prove their claim have produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, inquest report along with sketch, PM report and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 8.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.3 has relied on the judgments reported in:
MFA No. 24117/2013 between The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Revanappa and another wherein it is held that the claimants are under the onus of discharging the burden of proving the rash and negligent driving by the driver of vehicle.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Revanappa and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly in this case the initial burden is on the petitioners to prove the alleged negligence of the rider of offending motor cycle.
9. As per the documents produced by the petitioner Ex.P1- FIR is came to be registered on the basis of first information given by the brother of the deceased.
In the said complaint, the first informant alleged the rash and negligent riding by the rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-08-X-8489.
The Ex.P3 is spot mahazar and Ex.P4 is rough sketch.
As per the contents of Ex.P3 & 4 the accident spot is in the left side and the road is of curve road.

In the Ex.P2 complaint it is alleged that the said Thulasi Kumar was pillion rider and the motor cycle was ridden by one Murugesh who rode the said motor cycle in rash and negligent manner and thereby the pillion rider Thulasi Kumar got slip and fell on the road.
10. The alleged accident is dated 09-02-2022 and the complaint was came to be registered on 11-02-2022 at about 5.25 p.m. after the death of Thulasi Kumar.

Further as per Ex.R2 police intimation and Ex.R3 MLC register extract it is stated that the said thulasi Kumar was brought to their hospital on 09-02-2022 at about 6.14 p.m. which alleged history of RTA with self fall from two wheeler at around 5.30 p.m. near KGF road.
Thereby the main contention of the respondent No.3 insuance company is that it is the self fall accident but the false complaint is created by implicating one Murugesh as rider.
11. At the out set there is no serious dispute in respect of Thulasi Kumar getting injuries in an RTA and death of Thulasi Kumar due to the said injuries sustained by him in the RTA dated 09-02-2022.

But the serious point for consideration and dispute is whether it is self fall accident caused by the deceased himself or whether at the time of accident one Murugesh was really riding the motor cycle and the deceased was a pillion rider.
12. On this point the PW.1 being the wife of the deceased examined herself and filed examination in chief in support of her case.
She deposed that one Murugesh was riding the motor cycle and her husband was the pillion rider.
When the PW.1 is cross-examined she denied the suggestion of riding of the motor cycle by her husband.

It is very important to note that admittedly the PW.1 is not an eye witness to the accident and she is deposing on the basis of evidence or information gathered by Nandini vs Janardhan M on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125286666/
4 others on the fact of accident.

13. To prove that one Murugesh was the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA.08.X.8489, the petitioners summoned the said Murugesh and upon service of summons Murugesh appeared before this court and examined on oath as PW.2.
The said Murugesh deposed that he was riding the motor cycle and the Thulasi Kumar was the pillion rider and the said accident is caused by the negligence of Thulasi Kumar.
The PW.2 admitted and deposed that he was riding the motor cycle.

Further in corroboration to this point if we see the Ex.R2 police intimation and Ex.R3 MLC register extract which shows that the Thulasi Kumar was brought to their hospital at about 6.17 p.m of 09-02-2022 who was accompanied by Murugesh who is PW.2.

The history, place, time and date of accident is also mentioned in Ex.R3 wherein as per the information available in Ex.R3 the said Thulasi Kumar got injuries around 5.30 p.m in RTA near KGF road, 1 km away from Bangarpet.
The entries in Ex.P3 & P2 were made at 6.17 p.m. of the very same day.
Thus within 45 minutes of the alleged accident the said Thulasi Kumar was brought to the hospital who was accompanied by PW.2.
Thus it is undisputed fact that PW.2 was with the deceased Thulasi Kumar when he brought to the hospital.

On considering these points it is argued by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the Murugesh was riding and the deceased Thulasi Kumar was the pillion rider, as such within 45 minutes of accident the PW.2 Murugesh able to take the deceased Thulasi Kumar to the hospital.
14. No doubt that in the Ex.R3 it is written that the Thulasi Kumar got injuries in an RTA by self fall in two wheeler.
The PW.2 deposed before this court that he was riding the motor cycle and without his fault Thulasi Kumar fell down from the motor cycle.

15. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 2 days in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought and the false implication of driver and vehicle.
It is very important to note that not every delay would move this tribunal to view the case of the petitioners doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 09-02-2022, but the FIR was lodged on 11.02.2022 and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after 2 days of occurrence of the accident.

But the informant has clearly narrated in Ex.P-2 complaint as to why the FIR was lodged belatedly by narrating that soon after the accident the deceased Thulasi Kumar was taken for treatment to R L Jalappa hospital, Kolar and as he was in ICU in critical condition the complaint was lodged after his death on 11-02-2022.
The said explanation offered by the informant for delaying the lodging of the FIR is plausible.
Because as per the evidence available on record the Thulasi Kumar after the accident was taken to R L Jalappa hospital admitted in ICU and his condition was critical.

Perhaps the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, has observed thus:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

entities.text: Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Lodging of FIR certainly proves Nandini vs Janardhan M on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125286666/
5 factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me)
Hence the delay of 2 days itself, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint and it cannot be considered as inordinate.

16. It is interesting to note that no doubt the FIR was lodged belatedly, but in all the medical records, it is clearly mentioned that the history narrated to the doctors by injured at the very first instance, as can be seen from Ex.R2 police intimation and Ex.R3 MLC register extract is that the injuries were sustained in an RTA involving a motor cycle on 09-02-2022 at about 5.30 p.m near KGF road, 1 km away from Bangarpet and also at the time of admission the said Thulasi Kumar was unconsious.
The Ex.R2 and R3 was prepared and issued on 09-02-2022 itself to the jurisdictional police station.
Thus the Ex.R2 and R3 helped the petitioners to prove that Thulasi Kumar got injuries in the RTA dated 09-02-2022.
Under such circumstances, this court is of the firm opinion that the delay is certainly backed by genuine reasons.

Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.2 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioners after the accident.
17. The fact of accident is established before this tribunal.

The Ex.P6 inquest report and Ex.P7 postmortem report also establishes that Thulasi Kumar died due to the injuries sustained by him in the said RTA dated 09-02-2022.
18.
The last point for consideration is whether Murugesh was riding and Thulasi Kumar was pillion rider or the said Thulasi Kumar was himself was a rider who got self fall.

The Ex.P8 is the charge sheet is filed against Murugesh by alleging that the said Murugesh was the rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-08-X-8489 wherein the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of the rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-08-X-8489.
The said Murugesh admitted before this tribunal that he was the rider at the time of accident.
As per Ex.R3 MLC register extract Murugesh was accompanied with the injured Thulasi Kumar at the time of admission of Thulasi Kumar in the hospital.

Merely because Murugesh has not got any injuries the opinion of the IO or investigation made by the IO Nandini vs Janardhan M on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125286666/
6 cannot be brush aside.

The entry in Ex.R3 that the injured Thulasi Kumar was brought by Murugesh to the hospital which helped the petitioners to show that Murugesh was the rider of the motor cycle and Thulasi Kumar was the pillion rider.
No doubt that the complaint was given after 2 days by alleging the negligence of Murugesh but the police intimation and MLC register extract was prepared on 09-02-2022 itself.

Even after issuance of police intimation by the police not made any efforts to visit the hospital to register the complaint is the lacuna of the investigating agency for which the petitioners cannot be held responsible.
As such as per the charge sheet PW.2 Murugesh was the rider who was negligent and made the deceased Thulasi Kumar from fell down from the motor cycle.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.3 further relied on the judgments reported in:
i) MFA No.1794/2013 (MV) between Smt Sowbhagyamma @ Bhagyamma and others Vs. M/s Bajaj Allianz General Ins. Co. Ltd., and another.
ii) MFA No.6992/2014 (MV) between M/s United India Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Vijay and another.

sentences.text: By relying on the above quoted judgments the learned counsel for the respondent No.3 vehemently argued that as the MLC register extract shows that the deceased has got injuries in an RTA of self fall, the same has to be considered and in the absence of involvement of the vehicle the case has to be dismissed.
I have carefully gone through with the judgments relied by the learned counsel for the respondent No.3.

In the present case on hand for the reasons discussed above the petitioners produced MLC register extract along with police intimation and also established the evidence regarding the involvement of the offending vehicle and also at the time of accident one Murugesh was the rider of the motor cycle.
No concrete materials placed by the insurance company to show that the said Murugesh was not the rider of the motor cycle.
Ex.P5 IMV report and the damages mentioned therein establishes the involvement of the vehicle.
As such in my humble opinion the judgments relied by the learned counsel for respondent No.3 are not applicable to the present case on hand.

19. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered Nandini vs Janardhan M on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125286666/
7 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: 20. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1 & PW.2, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-X-8489 resulting in the death of one Thulasi Kumar by sustaining injuries.
Therefore Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 21.
As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Thulasi Kumar died on 11.02.2023 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
22. As contended in the petition, that the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 & 3 are the parents of the deceased.
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased.

The petitioners to prove their relationship with the deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aadhar cards of petitioners with deceased which are marked at Ex.P.12 &
13.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhaar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.

23. As per these documents the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 & 3 are the parents of the deceased, but the respondents do not dispute the relationship of the petitioners with deceased.

24. In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioners is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioners being the wife and parents of the deceased are the dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, issue No.2 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:

8 25.

As held herein above, the petitioners proved that Thulasi Kumar died on 11.02.2022 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-08-X-8489.
26.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.

The petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P13- as per the said document the deceased was born on 03.02.1994,
the accident took place in the year-2022, If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 28 years.
Hence this court is accepting the age of the deceased as 28 years.
27. As stated in the petition deceased was working as team leader and earning Rs.20,000/-.

To prove the said fact, the petitioners have produced letter of appointment and pay slip, which are marked at Ex.P9 &
10.
But as per Ex.P10 pay slip the salary was used to be credited to the account of the deceased.
The account statement or the employer is not examined before this tribunal.
Hence the petitioners failed to establish that the deceased was working as team leader and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.

As such in the absence of evidence on income, the notional income of deceased is considered as Rs.15,500/-
p.m. as the accident is of the year 2022 and the annual income comes to Rs.1,86,000/- .
28.
As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 17.

Since the deceased left his wife and parents, it is considered that, there are three dependents of deceased,
hence 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.21,08,000/- (Rs.15,500/- X 12 X 17= Rs.31,62,000/- minus 1/3rd (Rs.10,54,000/-) =
Rs. 21,08,000/-).
29.

In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component."
30.

Once notional income is determined,
the effects of inflation would equally apply.
Further, no one would ever say that the improvements in skills that come with experience do not take place in the domain of work within the household.

It is worth nothing that, although not extensively discussed, this Court has been granting future prospects even in cases pertaining to notional income, as has been highlighted by my learned brother, Surya Kant, J., in Nandini vs Janardhan M on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125286666/
9

his opinion (Hem Raj V. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2018) 15 SCC 654:

31. As per the above decisions 40% out of loss of dependency has to be granted towards future prospects which would Rs.8,43,200/-.
32.

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.

sentences.text: The Petitioners are the wife and parents of the deceased Thulasi Kumar.
The wife petitioner No.1 lost her loving husband, companion at the age of 21 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him.
The petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the parents of the deceased and they lost their loving care taker.
Therefore they are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.44,000/each.
Rs.40,000/x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium.

Further, I inclined to award a sum of Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).
34.
TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES;
The petitioners have produced medical bills as per Ex.P11 for Rs.52,446/-.

By considering the nature of the injuries and the documents produced at Ex.R4 ie.,
inpatient case details the petitioners are entitled for the reimbursement for the said amount by rounding off the same for Rs. 52,450/- under the head of medical expenses.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:

Liability:- According to the petitioners the respondent No.1 is the R.C. owner,
respondent No.2 is the insurance policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.3 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-08-X-8489.
The respondent No.3 has not made out any grounds by showing the violation of policy conditions.

Hence, the respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners and the respondent No.3 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 & 2.
The petitioners are entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. except on the amount awarded under the head of future prospectus.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
36.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.
No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 09-02-2022, but the FIR was lodged on 11.02.2022 and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after 2 days of occurrence of the accident.
But the informant has clearly narrated in Ex.P-2 complaint as to why the FIR was lodged belatedly by narrating that soon after the accident the deceased Thulasi Kumar was taken for treatment to R L Jalappa hospital, Kolar and as he was in ICU in critical condition the complaint was lodged after his death on 11-02-2022.
The said explanation offered by the informant for delaying the lodging of the FIR is plausible.
Because as per the evidence available on record the Thulasi Kumar after the accident was taken to R L Jalappa hospital admitted in ICU and his condition was critical.
Hence the delay of 2 days itself, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint and it cannot be considered as inordinate.
Thus the Ex.R2 and R3 helped the petitioners to prove that Thulasi Kumar got injuries in the RTA dated 09-02-2022.
Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.2 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioners after the accident.
Merely because Murugesh has not got any injuries the opinion of the IO or investigation made by the IO Nandini vs Janardhan M on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125286666/
6 cannot be brush aside.
Even after issuance of police intimation by the police not made any efforts to visit the hospital to register the complaint is the lacuna of the investigating agency for which the petitioners cannot be held responsible.
In the present case on hand for the reasons discussed above the petitioners produced MLC register extract along with police intimation and also established the evidence regarding the involvement of the offending vehicle and also at the time of accident one Murugesh was the rider of the motor cycle.
No concrete materials placed by the insurance company to show that the said Murugesh was not the rider of the motor cycle.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased.
